message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – the simplest and most abundant element in the universe

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.008 u (average; protium ≈ 1.0079 u) |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (^1H), Deuterium (^2H, D), Tritium (^3H, T) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) |
| **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (≈ 0.00008988 g cm⁻³) |
| **Molar volume at STP** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| **State at room temperature** | Gas |
| **Color** | Colorless |
| **Odor** | Odorless |
| **Taste** | Tasteless |
| **Solubility in water** | Slightly soluble (~0.00018 g g⁻¹ at 25 °C) |
| **Acidity/Basicity** | Very weak acid (HF) when bonded to electronegative atoms; very weak base as H⁻ (hydride). |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; forms explosive mixtures with air (5–75 % H₂ in air). |
| **Reactivity** | Reacts with halogens, oxygen, metals (forming hydrides), acids (forming H₂ gas). |
| **Bonding** | Forms covalent bonds; typically diatomic (H₂) under normal conditions. |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR). |
| **Common compounds** | Water (H₂O), ammonia (NH₃), methane (CH₄), acids (e.g., HCl, H₂SO₄). |
| **Industrial uses** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), refining (hydroprocessing), ammonia synthesis (Haber process), metal processing, rocket propellant. |
| **Biological role** | Essential component of amino acids, nucleic acids, ATP, and many metabolic pathways. |

**Key Takeaways**

- Hydrogen is the lightest element, existing naturally as a diatomic gas (H₂).
- It has three stable isotopes; deuterium and tritium are used in nuclear fusion research.
- Its low boiling/melting points and high flammability make it useful as a clean fuel but require careful handling.
- In chemistry, hydrogen’s ability to form both acidic (proton donor) and basic (hydride) species makes it versatile in reactions.
